Count regression with a random intercept per cluster

Source: R/cntmix.R
cntmix.Rd

Fits the log-linear model of a count with a normal random intercept for each cluster, \(\log E[y_{ij} | u_j] = x_{ij}'\beta + u_j\), \(u_j \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\), with a Poisson or a negative binomial (variance mu + mu^2 / theta) response, by maximum likelihood with the Laplace approximation of each cluster's integral (Breslow and Clayton 1993), as 'glmmTMB' and 'lme4' fit it. It is the main model of Ruhela (2026): placement volatility on alert complexity with a random intercept per regional cluster.

Usage

cntmix(y, x, grp, fam = c("nb", "poisson"), w = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

y

The counts: whole numbers from 0.

x

The covariates: a data frame (factors and text enter as indicators of each level but the first) or a numeric matrix, one row per count; an intercept is added.

grp

The cluster of each count: labels, at least two clusters, one of them with two rows or more.

fam

"nb" or "poisson".

w

NULL or a weight from 0 for each count.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class cntmix, a list: coef, a data frame (term, est, se, z, p, irr, lo, hi; NA for a term that cannot be estimated); sigma, the standard deviation of the intercepts; theta (NA for Poisson); loglik, aic; fam, the family reported; n, ngrp; conv, the optimiser's code (0 when it converged); level; notes, why a term has no estimate (empty when every term has one).

Details

The algorithm: for given beta, log sigma (and log theta), each cluster's mode of the random intercept is found by Newton's method on its one-dimensional log-density, all clusters at once (O(n) per step, quadratic convergence); the Laplace approximation of the marginal log-likelihood is then a sum over clusters. The outer parameters are maximised by BFGS from the Poisson fit without random effects, and their standard errors are from the inverse of the numerically differentiated Hessian at the maximum.

When the negative binomial's theta runs off to the Poisson limit (above 1e6), its likelihood is flat in that direction and the Hessian is singular; the Poisson model is then reported, as it is the limit, with theta noted (fam says which). Fewer than two clusters, or clusters of one row each, are refused: the variance of the intercepts is then not identified.

A coefficient that cannot be estimated is NA with its standard error, test and interval, and notes says why, never a standard error of 0: a column aliased with the others (a constant, or a combination of other columns, found by the QR decomposition of the design before the fit, which drops it as stats::lm() does); a 0/1 column all of whose counts on one side are 0 (separation: its rate ratio is 0 or infinite, and so is the intercept's when the zeros are where the column is 0); and an estimate whose variance from the Hessian is not a positive number.

References

Breslow, N. E. and Clayton, D. G. (1993). Approximate inference in generalized linear mixed models. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 88(421), 9-25. doi:10.1080/01621459.1993.10594284

Brooks, M. E., Kristensen, K., van Benthem, K. J., Magnusson, A., Berg, C. W., Nielsen, A., Skaug, H. J., Maechler, M. and Bolker, B. M. (2017). glmmTMB balances speed and flexibility among packages for zero-inflated generalized linear mixed modeling. The R Journal, 9(2), 378-400. doi:10.32614/RJ-2017-066

Examples

set.seed(2)
g <- rep(1:12, each = 40)
d <- rbinom(480, 1, 0.3)
y <- rpois(480, exp(-1 + 0.4 * d + rnorm(12, 0, 0.5)[g]))
cntmix(y, data.frame(d = d), g, fam = "poisson")
#> cntmix: poisson counts with a random intercept per cluster
#> 480 counts in 12 clusters; sigma 0.5101; log-likelihood -459.3308
#>         term     est     se      z         p    irr     lo    hi
#>  (Intercept) -0.8465 0.1695 -4.994 5.919e-07 0.4289 0.3077 0.598
#>            d  0.4339 0.1215  3.573 3.535e-04 1.5433 1.2164 1.958
